name: Ben Ray Luján

issue_poll.name: Albuquerque Journal Poll (Research & Polling Inc.), Aug 21-28, 2026, 516 likely voters; plus Emerson College NM poll Apr 18-19, 2026 and Conservation in the West poll (Colorado College) Jan 2-18, 2026
issue_poll.note: Ranks 1-4 and 6 from the Journal Poll open-ended 'biggest concern facing your family' question (inflation/cost of living 47%, health care 17%, financial insecurity 16% merged into cost of living, crime 8%, education 7%, immigration 6%); same poll found 82% call crime a serious issue. Ranks 5 and 7 added from Emerson's most-important-issue question among likely primary voters (housing affordability 9%, threats to democracy 7%; https://emersoncollegepolling.com/new-mexico-2026-poll/). Ranks 8-10 from Conservation in the West NM sample share calling each an extremely/very serious problem (inadequate water supplies 66%, wildfires 63%, funding cuts to public lands 58%; https://www.coloradocollege.edu/other/stateoftherockies/conservationinthewest/2026-poll-data/2026-state-of-the-rockies%20deck%20FINAL.pdf). The October 1-9 Journal Poll reported no issue questions. Ranking across polls with different question types is a judgment call.

issues.detail: Lower fuel, food, electricity and farm input costs; opposes sweeping tariffs but names no action.
Protect access to affordable health care; unnamed home and elder care legislation in drafting.
Strengthen public safety; kids grow up in safe, strong communities.
Build a pipeline from colleges and trade schools to jobs; no program or funding named.
Vote against the SAVE Act and the latest Republican voter ID / proof-of-citizenship bill.
Protecting land, air and water is at the top of his list; no measures named.
Oppose broad sales of federal public lands in New Mexico; oppose new limits on public access.

plan_caveats: Source NM's Sept 11, 2026 candidate questionnaire (likely the most detailed 2026 source), the campaign Priorities page (benraylujan.com/priorities), and several Albuquerque Journal articles could not be fetched; the three None ratings and several Vague ratings could change if those pages hold specifics.
Luján did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 survey; the Oct 22 KRWG/PBS forum had no transcript available.

Official Senate office actions in 2026 (e.g., pledged no votes on DHS/ICE funding in January, ACA tax credit push, Hermits Peak wildfire funding) were treated as in-office record, not campaign promises, and not counted.

Elections rated Concrete because opposing named bills (SAVE Act, GOP voter ID bill) is checkable by votes; it is opposition rather than a proposal. His call to 'modernize' the filibuster was too vague to record.
Public lands rated Partial: opposition to 'broad' sales is a clear direction but qualified, with no named bill.

Issue ranking merges three polls with different question types; data centers (strong opposition in the Aug Journal Poll) and gas prices were considered but lacked a comparable salience measure. AI regulation and a congressional stock-trading ban were stated positions but not among the top 10 issues.
